planting.note: Set out a bare-root or container-grown Hahs shrub in early spring into moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; the cultivar is self-fertile, but planting a second seedling or cultivar nearby improves fruit set.

directions: Hahs is a named selection of American highbush cranberry prized above other cultivars for producing the largest fruit of any highbush cranberry, borne in heavy, drooping clusters that ripen bright red in fall and hang on well into winter. The berries carry high pectin content, making them especially well suited to homemade jam and jelly without added pectin, and their tart, cranberry-like flavor mellows after the first hard frost. Unlike many highbush cranberry selections, Hahs is self-fertile and will set a good fruit crop on its own, though a second plant nearby increases yield further. It is not fussy about soil and tolerates full sun to partial shade, forming a rounded, multi-stemmed shrub more compact than the wild species. Extremely cold-hardy, it thrives through northern Great Plains and upper Midwest winters that few other fruiting shrubs survive; prune out the oldest canes at the base every few years to keep it vigorous and productive.
